findings.claim: The words 'paradise' (jannah) and 'hell' (jahannam) each occur 77 times.
findings.corpus_and_method: Method not stated by the source.
findings.our_note:
Strict singular forms (الجنة/جنة with prefixes: الجنة 56 + جنة 18 + وجنة 2 + بالجنة 1) = 77; جهنم substring 77. The جنة substring alone is 78 — the one extra token is أَجِنَّةٌ (ajinnah, 'fetuses', 53:32), not a form of 'garden' (an earlier draft of this note called it a construct form). The popular 77/77 claim counts singular 'garden' only. Counting every garden by root/lemma (QAC lemma jan~ap: singular 71 + plural جنات 69 + dual 7) gives 147 — that is the 147 in Agent 1's heaven/hell pair (147:77), while hell (jahannam) is 77 under both rules. Both numbers are true under different stated rules: singular garden vs all gardens.

Methods pass (2026-11-08): confirmed→differs: 12 of the 77 exact surface forms are not 'garden' — جِنَّة (jinn/madness, 10 tokens) and جُنَّة (shield, 2). Sense-correct garden counts are 65 (unsuffixed singular), 70 (QAC lemma singular), 147 (all gardens) — none is 77. Hell is 77 under both rules.

findings.claim: The word 'day' (yawm) occurs 365 times, matching the days of a (Gregorian) year.

findings.scholar_method: Yahya's page states the qualifier: 'The word faith (iman) (without genitive) is repeated 25 times throughout the Qur'an as is also the word infidelity (kufr).' Units: the nouns إيمان / كفر, with the genitive excluded. What '(without genitive)' means in practice is reconstructed below (see verification note); the qualifier itself is verbatim from the source.
findings.exceptions: Genitive in Arabic covers the possessive pronoun suffixes (إيمانهم/إيمانكم/كفرهم -- the suffix is a genitive pronoun). Bare (unsuffixed) tokens: iman 25 (GEN-case 12 + ACC-case 11 + NOM-case 2); kufr 25 (ACC-case 14 + GEN-case 10 + NOM-case 1). Suffixed tokens excluded: iman 20, kufr 12. The alternative reading -- excluding all GEN-case tokens -- gives 21 (iman) and 20 (kufr) and does NOT reproduce 25. The circulating list (quranic-miracles.com) gives iman/kufr as 17, not 25.

verification_scholar_rule.note: Reconstructed implementation of the stated qualifier: bare (unsuffixed) noun forms give exactly 25/25 (QAC LEM <iyma`n bare 25; LEM kufor bare 25). Both words occur together in several of the same verses (2:108, 3:167, 3:177, 9:23, 16:106, 49:7).
